assessment:
The table counts eight tutors and assumes you are hunting nineteen different kills. You are hunting one card. Stack 001 took the census: of the eight sacrifice outlets in this deck that cost no mana, exactly one — Yawgmoth, Thran Physician — also places a -1/-1 counter. He is the default wish almost everywhere in this book, and that is a strength rather than a rut.

Trust the depth and stop hoarding. You draw a tutor in 78.0% of games at a mean of turn 2.695, so fire the first one at the first hole in the census instead of saving it for a clever turn that may never arrive.

Name the card knowing its delivery speed. Demonic Tutor, Diabolic Intent, Grim Tutor and Survival of the Fittest put the wish in your hand now. Vampiric Tutor, Imperial Seal and Worldly Tutor put it on TOP — those are appointments, not arrivals, so fire the two instants at the end step before your untap and cut the transit to nothing. Green Sun's Zenith is the only one that pays tempo rather than charging it.

One standing order for every entry below. Nothing here fetches on the promise of the Blowfly kill, because no checker has ever signed that line. Go and get Blowfly Infestation when the grind wants another counter source. Never go and get it as a two-card win.

targets.scenario: Turn 3. Hapatra landed on turn 2 — she does in 9,970 of 10,000 goldfish runs — a Snake or two on the board, and nothing in hand that places counters more than once.
targets.why: Take the default wish and take it now. Stack 001's census is blunt: of the eight sacrifice outlets that cost no mana, he is the only one that also places a counter, so he is a card, a removal ping and a Snake on every activation. Never aim that counter at the creature you are sacrificing — it is the ability's only target, so it goes illegal on resolution and you lose the counter and the draw together. Aim at something else, or choose no target at all and just take the card.

targets.scenario: A free repeatable counter source is already running — Yawgmoth ticking, or the Druid loop live under Mikaeus — and three healthy life totals are the last thing between you and the game.
targets.why: Convert on placement, not on death, because placement is where your engine is loud. Stack 001 puts the Druid loop's steady state at four placements to one death per cycle, so the Spider drains the whole table four times where Zulaport Cutthroat drains it once. Take Cutthroat as the backup and rank Blood Artist under both — he bills one player.

targets.scenario: You are behind. Two wide boards across the table, your engine half-built, and real damage arriving next rotation.
targets.why: Fetch the rebuild rather than the reset. X counters on each creature triggers Hapatra once per creature, fills Nest of Scarabs, and hands Necroskitter every opposing creature that dies carrying one — so you come out of your own sweeper wider than you went in. Your 1/1s die too, and you should be happy about it: you already banked the trigger. It shuffles itself back in, so spend it and know you can find it again.

tutors.notes: Two mana, any card, no strings. This is the tutor you never save — point it at the census hole and cast it.

targets.scenario: Turn 3 with Hapatra out and a spare Snake standing around. Grim Haruspex or Blood Artist on the board makes it sweeter.
targets.why: Pay the additional cost with a body whose death already pays you. Sacrifice the Snake, collect the death triggers, take the one enabler the census says matters — the same wish as Demonic Tutor at roughly no cost. Sequence the sacrifice through your payoffs before you cast it, not after.

targets.scenario: Devoted Druid is on the battlefield and you have counted the table's creature removal and watched it get spent elsewhere.
targets.why: This is the closing wish, so schedule it like one. Mikaeus plus Devoted Druid is the deck's one verified true two-card infinite (stack 001): infinite deaths, placements, Snakes and drain, and explicitly not mana. He costs six against a mean 6.150 available on turn six, so fetch him on turn five and cast him on turn six rather than hoping both fit in one turn.

targets.scenario: You are one untap from the pivot and a single open answer would break the attempt.
targets.why: Buy the turn, and only the turn you actually go — hexproof and indestructible beat a targeted answer and a destruction wrath in the same breath. Do not lean on it against a Toxic Deluge effect: whether it saves a creature being killed by toughness reduction is an open question that deserves its own stack scenario, so play as if it does not.

targets.scenario: Turn 1, one green mana, an ordinary hand.
targets.why: Cast it for X equals one and buy yourself a bigger turn 2. Hapatra already lands on turn 2 in 9,970 of 10,000 runs; this is how she lands with company instead of alone. Take Birds of Paradise instead when your colours are awkward.

targets.scenario: Mikaeus, the Unhallowed is on the battlefield. Any table, any turn.
targets.why: Deploy the combo piece straight onto the battlefield for X equals two and skip the turn you would otherwise spend holding it — this is the only tutor in the book that does that. The loop needs no haste: the untap cost carries no tap symbol, so summoning sickness never touches it. Stack 001 has three green on the first pass and zero after, so take the mana once and then play the loop as deaths, Snakes and drain.

targets.scenario: A counter engine is running and the board needs to become a clock.
targets.why: Go get the drain at X equals three, and remember most tables forget Zenith reaches it. Every placement drains each opponent — four per Druid cycle off stack 001's steady state — and nobody points removal at a Spider until it is far too late.

tutors.notes: Zenith shuffles itself back in, so spending it early costs you nothing but the mana. Cast it at X equals one on turn 1 without agonising; the deck can find it again.

targets.scenario: Turn 3-4, no repeatable counter source in hand, and the cheaper tutors are spent or absent.
targets.why: Pay the three life for the enabler and never for a luxury. The surcharge is real in a deck that already bills you through Yawgmoth, Bitterblossom, Phyrexian Reclamation and three painlands, so cast this one on the turn the census hole is genuinely the enabler.

targets.scenario: The engine is running, bodies are flowing, and your hand is empty.
targets.why: Fetch the card that turns your board back into a grip. Every Snake, Insect, Faerie and Elf Warrior is a 1/1, so this is pay one, draw two, on repeat. When the board is ahead of the hand, take the engine over any single spell you could name instead.

targets.scenario: Turn 1 or 2, before the game has taken shape. It is sorcery speed and the wish arrives on your next draw, so it wants to be cast early rather than at the pivot.
targets.why: Schedule the enabler; do not spend the Seal like a real tutor. Cast it on turn 2 and Yawgmoth is in hand on turn 3 and on the battlefield turn 4, on curve, for two life you barely notice that early. Fire it late and you have announced the pivot a full turn out and handed the table a draw step to answer it.

targets.scenario: A wrath is coming — a control seat is holding up mana, your board is wide, and your untap is the rebuild turn.
targets.why: Put the rebuild on top the night before and stop guessing. If the wrath comes, you untap into counters on each creature, a Snake per creature, food for Nest of Scarabs and a collection for Necroskitter. If it does not come, you cast the table's best sweeper on your schedule instead of theirs.

targets.scenario: Any turn with {G} open and a spare creature card in hand — a dork whose job is done, a redundant body.
targets.why: Activate on the first turn you can and take the census answer, every time. The discard barely registers with Phyrexian Reclamation and Eternal Witness in the 99 to buy the card straight back. This is the most powerful card in the section because it is the only one that grants a wish more than once.

targets.scenario: Late game, six-plus mana in sight, the table's removal counted and already spent.
targets.why: Assemble across two activations rather than praying for a draw: Mikaeus now, Walking Ballista next. That package plus any free outlet is verified genuinely unbounded (stack 001), and it is three cards because Mikaeus's anthem keeps a counterless Ballista alive at 1/1 — so the outlet does the recycling. You already have eight of those.

targets.scenario: A creature table is going wide and Black Sun's Zenith is in your hand.
targets.why: Turn their board into yours: every creature an opponent controls that dies with a -1/-1 counter on it comes back under your control. Take the honest label with it — that read is oracle text with no stack scenario behind it, so plan around it and never promise it to yourself in a turn you have to win.

tutors.notes: Survival reveals each fetch. After the second activation the table knows exactly what you are assembling, so budget protection or politics from that moment rather than after the third.

targets.scenario: End step of the opponent before you, turn 2-3, engine incomplete.
targets.why: Fire it at the last legal moment and the top card is yours before anyone can act on the information — zero turns in transit, which is the entire card. It costs two life and your draw step, so spend it on the turn the answer matters and never on curiosity.

targets.scenario: You are behind, the aggro seat is lethal-adjacent, and rebuilding is not going to be enough.
targets.why: Reach for the panic button and sequence it as one. It places no counters, so Hapatra, Nest of Scarabs and Necroskitter all give you nothing — cast it for the board, not for value. Tutor at their end step so Deluge is in hand for your main phase, and pay the X out of a life total this deck already spends freely.

targets.scenario: A counter source is online, the pivot is next turn, and the kill needs a table-wide clock.
targets.why: Put it on top tonight, cast it for three tomorrow, and drain every opponent on every placement from then on — four per cycle on the Druid loop. Prefer it to Mikaeus when you want the clock without the attention; nobody holds up removal for a Spider.

targets.scenario: Turn 2, end of turn, one mana open, no counter source in hand.
targets.why: One mana at instant speed for the enabler, so fire it on the end step before your untap and the exposure is zero. The reveal is public: the table watches him coming, so hold a second body ready and expect the removal on the turn he lands.

targets.scenario: Mikaeus, the Unhallowed is on the battlefield with any free outlet — Ashnod's Altar, Viscera Seer, Carrion Feeder, take your pick of the eight.
targets.why: Close the game: Mikaeus plus Ballista plus a free outlet is verified unbounded at one damage a pass, no drain payoff required (stack 001). Remember why it needs the third card — the anthem keeps a counterless Ballista alive at 1/1, so the outlet does the recycling and the Ballista never gets to kill itself.

targets.scenario: Targeted removal just clipped your enabler and the tutor that found him is in the graveyard.
targets.why: Buy the card back and get a body doing it. Witness returns the tutor or the answered piece to your hand and is herself sacrifice fodder afterwards — two wishes for one draw step, and the second one is private.

gaps: Every default wish is the same card and the table learns that fast. Yawgmoth dies on sight against anyone competent, so decide your second fetch before the first one resolves. Devoted Druid under Mikaeus is the verified backup engine and Phyrexian Reclamation buys Yawgmoth back for {1}{B} and two life.

Three of these eight deliver to the top of your library, so the wish can die in transit to held interaction. Fire Vampiric Tutor and Worldly Tutor at the end step before your untap to cut the exposure to nothing, and treat the sorcery-speed Imperial Seal as an early-game card only.

No tutor here finds an artifact or enchantment answer, because none exists to find. Against a resolved prison piece the library has nothing for you — race, politick, or borrow somebody else's removal. These wishes make you faster; they cannot make you broader.

Point them at the engine and take the number the goldfish puts on it: modelled as wildcards, these eight take 'Mikaeus plus a free outlet' from 9.5% of games to 50.4%. They also take the Blowfly pairing from 16.3% to 66.7%, and you should refuse that trade every time — no checker has signed the line, so a tutor pointed at it is a card spent on a maybe.
